hypothesis: The expanded pilot sleeve now has more eligible names than its single concurrent slot can hold. Replacing input-order pilot slot selection with trade-quality priority should improve forward pilot capital allocation without expanding the core universe or adding noisy tickers.

alpha_hypothesis.statement: When multiple pilot candidates are simultaneously tradeable, the single pilot slot should go to the strongest scored signal rather than the first signal produced by the engine.

related_failed_or_limited_experiments.summary: HOOD/RBLX/SOFI were accepted into the bounded pilot sleeve from 2026-05-08, increasing competition for the single pilot slot without changing core historical metrics.
Consumer digital platform basket was positive but unstable; direct core promotion was rejected.
Simple governance gates did not stabilize the consumer platform basket enough for core promotion.
Broad core candidate-quality ordering was rejected; this experiment is narrower because it only ranks already-scaled pilot candidates competing for one pilot slot.

historical_context.mechanism_insight_check: This does not repeat rejected LLM soft-ranking, C/earnings re-enable, short-pressure, options, state-surface pruning, event-source pruning, RS20 leader, gap-up, or far-from-earnings sizing experiments. It also avoids broad universe expansion by allocating a pre-existing pilot slot better.

why_not_other_alpha: LLM soft-ranking and veto attribution remain data-limited, so another LLM strategy change would be underpowered.
C/earnings revalidation recently regressed all windows after snapshot coverage improved.
Recent event-overlay and state-surface changes are waiting on forward paper outcomes or failed Gate 4.
Adding more pilot tickers would increase noise; the live bottleneck is now which pilot candidate gets the single slot.
gate_4_assessment: Core fixed-window metrics are intentionally unchanged because pilot eligibility starts after all canonical windows. The experiment is accepted as a production-aligned forward pilot allocation improvement, not as a historical core-alpha improvement.
decision_reason: The policy is lower complexity than expanding the pilot universe, lives in shared pilot_sleeve.py, is consumed by both production and backtester pilot paths, and leaves canonical core metrics unchanged.
next_review_trigger: Review after enough closed pilot outcomes to compare selected pilot candidates against pilot_slot_sliced_signals and cash/core alternatives.
main_risk: A high trade_quality_score pilot signal can still be lower quality than a sliced pilot candidate if the score is stale or poorly calibrated for newly added pilot tickers.
